drhp.business: The Grob Tea Company Ltd owns and operates tea estates in Assam, cultivating and manufacturing black CTC and orthodox teas, as well as green tea. The company sells its tea primarily through auction centers and private sales to domestic buyers, with a portion directed to export markets. Its operations are vertically integrated from plantation to processing, relying on a large workforce across its estates.
drhp.end_markets: Domestic Indian market (auction centers and private sales)|Export markets
drhp.expansion: The Company has undertaken a comprehensive project called 'Project Work on Climate Change' (PWCC) to mitigate the ill-effects of erratic weather and improve the micro-climate around its tea gardens. As part of this initiative, the capacity and efficiency of existing irrigation sets are being improved to a large extent to minimize the impact of early drought. The MD&A notes that climate change has altered monsoon patterns, leading to longer dry spells and shorter periods of heavy rain, which this project aims to address. risks.note: Tea crop is totally rain-dependent; global warming causes high ambient temperatures and erratic rainfall (long dry spells, short heavy rains), jeopardizing production across all tea-growing regions, especially North East India.
risks.risk: Climate change and erratic weather patterns

risks.note: Tea is a labour-intensive industry; shortage of labour during peak season, substantial increases in labour costs, high social costs, and other input costs remain a major structural concern.
Organized sector production share dropped to 43% (down 3% YoY) while STG share rose to 57%, a steadily continuing structural shift that pressures organized players.
risks.risk: Increasing dominance of small tea growers (STGs) and declining organized sector share

risks.note: Cheap imported teas getting blended with domestic production is a serious concern that can undermine domestic price stability and quality perception.
risks.risk: Import of cheap tea varieties mixing with domestic production

risks.note: Despite higher exports, much higher domestic retention led to a 9% drop in average Assam CTC price realization; profitability is highly sensitive to sale price fluctuations.
Record exports of 280 M kgs (up 9% YoY) are expected to rise further only if the geopolitical situation remains favourable, making export-led market stability conditional.
